result.title: When Calibration Data Matter in Sub-4-Bit Language Model Quantization
result.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. 10 pages main text, 47 pages total including references, checklist, and appendices
result.summary: Low-bit post-training quantization reduces language-model memory but can sharply degrade downstream task accuracy. Calibration usually relies on generic text, but when task-informed data recover accuracy and which quantizers benefit remain poorly understood. We introduce FragCal-DC, which supplements generic text with training documents from task families with low retention of full-precision accuracy in a two-bit scan. We use a two- to four-bit sweep to locate functional regimes and four-seed calibration comparisons to evaluate six data-dependent methods across six dense models (1.7B-8B) and ten tasks. At their lowest tested functional bit widths, iterative SignRound V2 and OmniQuant improve at two bits, whereas single-pass GPTQ and AWQ show small mean responses at three bits. At two bits, SignRound V2 gains 1.83 percentage points in mean ten-task accuracy over generic-text calibration across six models. At 70 billion parameters, GPTQ and SignRound V2 both improve at two bits, with functional generic-calibration baselines. For two-bit SignRound V2, task-level controls show that recovery concentrates on families included in calibration, while incorrect answer designations retain about 90% of the mean accuracy gain. Changes in reconstruction error do not consistently track accuracy gains. These findings support task-informed calibration as a design principle for preserving downstream accuracy in low-bit quantization.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究低比特（2–4 bit）训练后量化中校准数据的作用，提出 FragCal-DC：先用二比特扫描找出全精度精度保留较差的任伤族，再用其训练文档补充通用文本校准，并在 6 个稠密模型、10 个任务及 70B 模型上比较六种量化方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 任务相关校准数据能恢复下游精度、且重建误差与精度增益不一致，可供核查 LVR 中压缩 latent 状态或视觉证据时如何选择校准/监督信号并避免以重建误差代替任务效果。
